title: Children's Bedtime Stories (Ages 3–4)
summary: Original, gentle, audio-first bedtime stories for children ages 3 to 4, primarily age three. Thirty-three standalone stories use one narrator, with playful journeys, small discoveries, everyday kindness, and quiet endings. There is no requirement that every story teach a lesson. Parent notes with source links and clear evidence limits are not spoken. No character voice acting, music, or sound effects are needed.
assumed_background: Designed for listeners ages 3–4; no prior familiarity with the characters or other episodes required.

lectures.title: Moss and the Missing Blanket
lectures.description: A bedtime search for a favorite blue blanket, ending with a remembered afternoon game.

lectures.title: The Little Cloud That Couldn't Settle
lectures.description: A drifting cloud discovers how to rest without stopping the wind.

lectures.title: Nia and the Moonlight Garden
lectures.description: A child and her grandmother identify three small nighttime sounds before returning to bed.

lectures.title: Moss and the Two Shovels
lectures.description: Moss keeps using his shovel; Pip finds another way to play, and the friends build a small world side by side.

lectures.title: The Footprints by the Pond
lectures.description: Pip and Moss make guesses about marks beside a pond, then watch a small duck drag a twig through the mud.

lectures.title: Pip's Tower Falls Down
lectures.description: A fallen block tower disappoints Pip; after a break and help with one step, he builds a different little house.

lectures.title: The Hedgehog Who Didn't Say Hello
lectures.description: Moss takes a missed greeting personally but learns that Hazel was occupied in the wind.

lectures.title: The Little Bird Who Needed Help
lectures.description: Tavi tries to hang a leaf curtain, asks Mama Bird to steady one side, and completes the job.

lectures.title: The Very Important Puddle
lectures.description: Pip plays in a puddle, Hazel notices the sky reflected in it, and Moss finds a dry way around.

lectures.title: Pip's Very Small Parade
lectures.description: Pip marches with a red leaf; friends join him, and the parade accidentally gives a snail a splendid hat.

lectures.title: Nia and the Backward Pajamas
lectures.description: A backward pajama top leads to slipper mittens, a very serious teddy bear, and a pretend moon in a pocket.

lectures.title: Otis and the Leaf Letter
lectures.description: A garden snail carries a little picture-letter past a pebble hill and grass forest to invite Hazel to watch the evening sky.

lectures.title: Pip's Pillow Orchestra
lectures.description: Friends find a soft thump, a puff, a rustle, and a tap, then notice the quieter sounds around them.

lectures.title: Hazel's Hat Shop
lectures.description: Hazel tries hats on a watering can, a pumpkin, a fence post, and eventually a very fashionable mouse.

lectures.title: Nia's Carpet Sea
lectures.description: A blanket becomes a sea, a towel becomes a mountain, and a stuffed bear finds a quiet bay for a nap.

lectures.title: Nia's Cardboard Moon Mission
lectures.description: A cardboard-box rocket makes a very quiet pretend trip to the moon and brings a present made from a blue sock.

lectures.title: Pip and the Very Long Goodnight
lectures.description: Pip tries to say goodnight to every object, pebble, and leaf, then remembers one sleepy mouse.

lectures.title: Moss and the Wobbly Pancake
lectures.description: Moss and Aunt Juniper make pancakes shaped like an elephant, a boot, a moon, and a turtle.

lectures.title: Hazel's Museum of Ordinary Things
lectures.description: Hazel opens a tiny museum containing a stone, a leaf window, a pine cone, and a surprise gift shop.

lectures.title: Otis and the Leaf Umbrella
lectures.description: Otis enjoys the rain, Pip dislikes wet socks, and a broad leaf makes the walk home easier.

lectures.title: Tavi's Nest of Soft Things
lectures.description: Tavi searches for a comfy resting spot, testing grass and a crinkly leaf with help from Mama Bird.

lectures.title: Luma and the Underwater Garden
lectures.description: Luma the octopus builds a sand garden with pebbles, ribbons of seaweed, and bubbles that keep rising.

lectures.title: Puff and the Too-Many Pockets
lectures.description: A cloud with seven pockets collects a paper crown, a cookie, a feather, and even a yawn.

lectures.title: Reed and the Star in the Pond
lectures.description: Reed the otter notices a star reflected in the pond and follows changes when a leaf and breeze pass.

lectures.title: The Tallest Hat in Mushroom Village
lectures.description: A beetle builds a hat too tall for any doorway; it becomes a strange little roof for village visitors.

lectures.title: The Night Train to Pillow Mountain
lectures.description: A child imagines a wooden train traveling over Button Bridge through Blanket Meadow to a pillow-shaped mountain.

lectures.title: The Cave That Giggled Back
lectures.description: Fern the little goat and Grandpa discover a soft echo outside a shallow cave, then settle into listening.

lectures.title: Della and the Daisy Sneeze
lectures.description: A friendly dragon sneezes daisies into a picnic; her friends find the flowers very funny.

lectures.title: The Little Red Wagon's Holiday
lectures.description: Nia takes her everyday garden wagon on a small holiday with Grandpa, all the way to the bean patch.

lectures.title: The Upside-Down Picnic Map
lectures.description: Moss and Hazel follow a picture map, notice the pond on the wrong side, and turn the paper around.

lectures.title: Lina and the Lantern Shadow
lectures.description: A little moth makes an enormous playful shadow beside a softly lit porch and discovers whose shape it is.

lectures.title: The Giant's Small Quilt
lectures.description: A mouse offers a little patchwork quilt to a giant, who finds it makes an excellent blanket for one chilly toe.

lectures.title: The Stars' Small Camping Trip
lectures.description: Three make-believe stars camp between clouds with a tiny spoon, pretend moonberry soup, and an unhurried goodnight.
